entries.guide.chip.tips: What can I do about my results?
entries.guide.tpl.tips.intro: Here are some ideas for the areas to work on first.
entries.guide.tpl.tips.none: All the areas you answered are in the recommended range. These habits help you stay there.
entries.ga.tobacco.no_reported_risk.why: Not using tobacco protects your heart, lungs and blood pressure.
entries.ga.tobacco.no_reported_risk.tips: Keep it that way, and stay away from other people's smoke where you can.
entries.ga.tobacco.attention.why: Tobacco in any form raises the chance of heart disease, stroke, lung disease and some cancers. The benefits of stopping start within weeks.
entries.ga.tobacco.attention.tips: If you want to cut down or stop, choose a day to start, tell someone you trust, and ask at your health centre about support to stop. Every time you choose not to use tobacco helps.
entries.ga.alcohol.lower_risk.why: Drinking little or no alcohol helps your liver, your blood pressure and your sleep.
entries.ga.alcohol.lower_risk.tips: If you drink, keep it occasional, eat when you drink, and have water in between.
entries.ga.alcohol.attention.why: Drinking often, or a lot at one time, raises blood pressure and the chance of liver disease, injuries and some cancers.
entries.ga.alcohol.attention.tips: Try a few alcohol-free days each week, choose smaller drinks, and switch between alcohol and water or juice. A health worker can talk it through with you, without judgement.
entries.ga.activity.meets.why: Regular activity strengthens your heart, helps with weight and blood pressure, and gives you more energy.
entries.ga.activity.meets.tips: Keep it going. Walking, sport, dancing and active work all count.
entries.ga.activity.below.why: Regular activity strengthens your heart, helps with weight and blood pressure, and gives you more energy.
entries.ga.activity.below.tips: Short bouts count. A brisk ten-minute walk, taking the stairs, walking part of your journey instead of taking a moto, or dancing to a few songs all add up.
entries.ga.diet.meets.why: Fruit and vegetables give your body fibre, vitamins and minerals that protect your heart.
entries.ga.diet.meets.tips: Keep adding them to every meal. Local fruit and vegetables in season are often the most affordable.
entries.ga.diet.below.why: Fruit and vegetables give your body fibre, vitamins and minerals that protect your heart.
entries.ga.diet.below.tips: Add one more serving at a time: a banana or avocado with breakfast, dodo, isombe or cabbage with lunch, or a piece of fruit as a snack.
entries.ga.bmi.underweight.why: Being below the healthy range can mean your body is not getting enough energy and nutrients.
entries.ga.bmi.underweight.tips: Regular meals with beans, eggs, milk, groundnuts or fish can help. If your weight has dropped without trying, it is worth seeing a health worker.
entries.ga.bmi.normal.why: A weight in the healthy range lowers the chance of high blood pressure and diabetes.
entries.ga.bmi.normal.tips: Regular activity and balanced meals help you stay here.
entries.ga.bmi.overweight.why: Weight above the healthy range raises the chance of high blood pressure, diabetes and joint pain over time.
entries.ga.bmi.overweight.tips: Focus on habits rather than quick weight loss: more vegetables, fewer sugary drinks and fried snacks, and a little more movement each day.
entries.ga.bmi.obesity.why: Weight well above the healthy range makes high blood pressure, diabetes and heart disease more likely.
entries.ga.bmi.obesity.tips: Small, steady changes to habits work best. A health worker can check your blood pressure and blood sugar and help you plan.
entries.ga.waist.not_increased.why: Your waist size is in the range linked with a lower chance of diabetes and heart disease.
entries.ga.waist.not_increased.tips: Activity and balanced meals help keep it that way.
entries.ga.waist.increased.why: Fat stored around the waist is linked with a higher chance of diabetes and heart disease.
entries.ga.waist.increased.tips: Moving every day and having fewer sugary drinks and fried foods help reduce it.
entries.ga.waist.substantially_increased.why: A much larger waist size is linked with a clearly higher chance of diabetes and heart disease.
entries.ga.waist.substantially_increased.tips: Steady changes to habits help, and a health worker can check your blood sugar and blood pressure.
entries.ga.bp.normal.why: Blood pressure in the normal range puts less strain on your heart and blood vessels.
entries.ga.bp.normal.tips: Stay active, go easy on salt, and have it checked again from time to time.
entries.ga.bp.high_normal.why: Blood pressure a little above normal can rise further over time, usually without any symptoms.
entries.ga.bp.high_normal.tips: Less salt, more fruit and vegetables, regular activity and less alcohol all help. Have it checked again the next time you visit a health centre.
entries.ga.bp.hypertension_range.why: One reading is not enough to know, so a reading in this range needs to be confirmed.
entries.ga.bp.hypertension_range.tips: Have it measured again at a health centre on another day. Until then, less salt and regular activity help.
